title: Perfectman Director contract
description: Generated from crates/sim/src/director.rs (proto 2). Do not edit by hand: run `cargo test -p tilehouse-sim director_schema`.

sidecar_to_hotel.description: Every frame also carries `seq` (a `u64` from 1 per connection and direction) beside `t`; see [`SidecarFrame`] and [`HotelFrame`]. It is left out here so the unions stay named types.

ActReason.description: `act_done.reason`: a blocked reason or an abort reason. `kill_switch` and `calm_room` are both.

oneOf.description: Dancing on the spot until stopped. Styles 1 to 4: Hab-Hop, Pogo-Mogo, Duck-Funk, The Rollie.
Dozing off, eyes shut, until the player does anything.
Holds up a sign, styles 0 to 17.
Ends a dance or an idle.
Shows a face, `style` 0..=5 (`perfectman::Face`). Allowed while walking; clears itself.
Turns in place to a direction, `style` 0..=7.
`furni`: the hotel resolves the seat tile and walks there. `floor`: sit on open floor.
`to` is an avatar id for a whisper. Text is at most 200 chars; links and markdown are stripped.
Same validity as `Room::act`. Not for expressions or turns: use `Expression` and `Face`.
Turns in place. Exactly one of `dir` (0..=7), `target` or `tile` is set.

pair.description: The sidecar's id for this act, echoed in `pair_reaction`.

oneOf.description: Emotion cues such as the `Love` and `Raincloud` effects. The sidecar restores the Actor's own effect afterwards by sending `appearance` again; the hotel keeps the last value (checklist 8).
A drama act (dialect 2 only; `act-contract.md` section 2). In a dialect 1 session this frame is unparseable and takes the `director_reject` path (NEG-5, ACT-1).

act_id.description: `^[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]{1,32}$`, unique within the run for its whole life.

intensity.description: `0..=1`; absent means the verb's default. Selects the impact class.

with.description: An avatar in the actor's room: required for the targeted verbs, forbidden for the solo ones.

oneOf.description: Reserved: not frozen until hand-item sprites exist (D33). The hotel answers `bad_message`.

ActorErrorCode.description: `actor_error.code`, plus the section 9 table of the doc.

oneOf.description: A permadeath actor retired at a scene cut (DEATH-7). Dialect 2 only.

ApiError.description: Error body of every authoring and admin route: `400 bad_request`, `401`, `422 bad_scenario`, `503 llm_unavailable`, `504 timeout`.

AutolookRequest.description: `catalog` is the constrained figure list the hotel supplies, one figure string per entry.

action.description: A dance or a doze under way, which people coming into the room are shown. Walking ends it.

ai.description: An AI Actor: the client draws a badge. Never sent to the Director (D43).

dir.description: 0 is north-west on screen (towards -y), increasing clockwise in tile space.

effect.description: Worn effect library name, empty for none.

face.description: The current expression (`perfectman::Face` style, 0 is neutral), so late joiners match.

figure.description: A `type:lib` figure string, empty for the procedural palette look.

oneOf.description: Dancing on the spot, set by games such as the chair dance.

BatchFailure.description: Why one step of a `Batch` was refused.

BlockedReason.description: Why a gate refused an accepted command (`outcome:"blocked"`), in no order.

Both.description: The only value of `motion.who` besides an avatar id.

rank.description: 2 to 10, then 11 jack, 12 queen, 13 king, 14 ace.

ChatImage.description: A picture, animated GIF or clip attached to a message. The file is served from `assets/chat/<id>/`.

oneOf.description: What a character thinks. Delivered only to Audience in a cinematic run (D30), always logged.
Narrator line. Shown as a lower-third to Audience, never as a bubble.

ChipAnswer.description: How a human answered a consent chip, including silence.

ChipChoice.description: What a human can press on the chip (`act_reply.choice`, `act_prompt.choices`).

ConsentFamily.description: The label set of a chip.

Downgrade.description: Table steps that were skipped or replaced (`act_done.downgraded`). `chat` is REA-9's muted line, which the table of section 3.6 does not list (spec defect, see `docs/perfectman/decisions.md`).

oneOf.description: They declined your request recently.
You've blocked this person, so you can't send them a request.
The room is in the middle of a game, so it can't be rearranged.
Not in this position or place, such as dancing while sitting.
Too many actions too quickly.
You have to stand next to a game piece to use it.
Someone is already using that piece, or you played a moment ago.
That piece isn't a game, or not that game.
That picture doesn't exist, isn't yours, or pictures are switched off.
The message is part of the Perfectman contract and the server does not handle it yet.

Face.description: What an expression shows, as `Action::Expression` styles 0..=5.

Features.description: Optional parts of the game this server has switched on.

video.description: Players may also send MP4 clips. Off when the server has no ffmpeg or `CHAT_VIDEO=off`.

FitZoom.description: The literal `"fit"`: the room's own opening zoom.

Furni.description: Where on its wall a piece hangs, in screen pixels at the default zoom. A piece placed before walls had a pixel grid has both at 0, which means the middle of the tile's edge at the height its art was drawn for (`WALL_MOUNT_LEVELS` unless the piece has its own).

layer.description: Which of the flat pieces (rugs and wall pieces) that overlap is drawn over which: higher is nearer the viewer, and pieces with the same layer go by position and then by id.

off.description: The cell along the tile's edge, 1 to `WALL_CELLS`, or 0 for the middle of the edge.

rot.description: Quarter turns, 0..=3. Odd turns swap width and depth.

state.description: Which of the piece's states it's in. 0 is the resting one.

up.description: How high above the tile's floor the piece's origin is, in pixels, or 0 for its usual height.

z.description: How far up a stack it starts, in hundredths of a level above the floor. The server works this out when placing or moving it, and rooms from before stacking are all 0.

GameView.description: What the Games window shows about the game a room is hosting.

duration_secs.description: How long it runs, in seconds, for a game with a clock: the host's choice, or the default.

HelloDrama.description: What `hello.drama` tells a dialect 2 sidecar (NEG-2). Sent only with `PERFECTMAN_DRAMA` on.

dead.description: Every actor that is `fainted`, `dying` or `body`: a full replacement set, not a delta (NEG-8).

name.description: Untrusted when the room is not official: its owner wrote it.

section.description: The navigator section of an official room (`Featured`, `Casinos`, `Games`, `Perfectman`).

room_name.description: Untrusted: the room owner wrote it.

drama.description: The drama offer: vocabulary, chip and harm numbers, and the dead set (NEG-2, NEG-8).

proto_max.description: The highest dialect the hotel offers. Present only with `PERFECTMAN_DRAMA` on (NEG-2).

rooms.description: Rooms the sidecar may travel to: every official room (the Perfectman wing included) and each room a live run is in, at most `HELLO_ROOMS_MAX`. Absent from an older hotel.

untrusted_text.description: JSON paths of strings a stranger wrote (section 7.1).

oneOf.description: A reconnect that resumes a run bumps its epoch.

model.description: The model the admin picked for this run (D54). Link 1 of the chain for this run; the configured chain stays behind it as failover. Absent: the chain as configured.

oneOf.description: The hotel ended the run itself; no reply.

args.description: Command arguments, unparsed. `whisper` takes `<name> <text>` with a name that contains spaces quoted (D51): `"Ana Clara" hello`. `auto` pauses carry `idle`.

cid.description: Absent when the failing frame had none (for example an unknown `t`).

oneOf.description: The room mirror's first message. `layout.rows`, `walk` and `seats` are server-derived so the sidecar re-implements no rules. The public `Avatar.ai` is never set here (D43).

name.description: Untrusted: the room owner wrote it.

walk.description: `.` blocked or void, `0` open, `s` seat, `g` gate or portal; one string per row.

oneOf.description: One mirrored public message; `rev` goes up by exactly 1 per mirrored message in the room. Strings in `msg` that a stranger wrote (avatar names) are untrusted by the same rule as snapshots, without a per-frame list.
Every 2 s per subscribed room. Does not change `rev`.

mode.description: `say`, `shout` or `whisper`; a whisper is forwarded only when `to` is an Actor (D44).

untrusted.description: Always true: human chat is untrusted in-world speech (D22).

oneOf.description: The walk ended: finished, route stale or blocked. `x`,`y` is where the Actor stopped.
Replaces the `avatar_left`/`avatar_joined` pair for the sidecar's own Actor.

reason.description: Why a drama session's `pair` was refused (PAIR-1): `kill_switch`, `calm_room` or `cooldown`. Never set towards a dialect 1 session.

oneOf.description: An act was accepted and began (FRM-1). Dialect 2 only.

contact_in_ms.description: Planned `Tc - T0`; `null` when a chip decides.

target_opt_in.description: Present only when `with` is a human.

oneOf.description: Contact happened: the clock of REA-1 and REA-2.

owed.description: The only ground truth of what is owed (REA-2).

oneOf.description: The target or a witness visibly reacted.
The act ended, or was blocked or aborted. Always the last frame of an act (FRM-1).

answer.description: The chip answer; present iff a chip was shown.

oneOf.description: A consent chip was shown or answered (human target only).

answer.description: On `answered`; a timeout is `answer:"timeout"` at `shown.at + ttl_ms`.

oneOf.description: An actor started dying (DEATH-1). Humans never produce it.
A dead actor was restored by a scene cut (DEATH-7).

effect.description: The effect it had before it died; empty for none.

oneOf.description: A killed human is down for `ms` (DOWN-1).
The down state ended (DOWN-3). May follow `act_done`.
The scene changed; always the answer to a `scene_advance` (SCENE-2).
Opt-in, calm, pause and switch state of a room.

opt_in.description: Human ids in the room whose session opt-in is on.

ImpactClass.description: The impact class of an act (TBL-4). The wire spelling is one capital letter.

Job.description: `GET /api/admin/perfectman/jobs/{id}`. In memory on the hotel: lost on restart, kept 10 min.

stage.description: What a running job is doing now, for the AI jobs ("research", "build"). Absent for the rest.

MediaKind.description: What an attachment is. Both `thumb` and `full` exist for every kind; the thumb is always a still.

oneOf.description: A still picture.
An animated GIF. Its full file is the animation.
An MP4 clip.

MotionWho.description: `motion.who`: an avatar id, or `"both"` (the actor and the target).

Origin.description: Who asked for an act: the model, the director or the scenario's author.

Outcome.description: What came up, for showing to the room.

OverlayEnd.description: How an overlay ends besides a number of milliseconds.

OverlayUntil.description: `overlay.until`: after that many ms, at the next scene cut, or when `act_overlay_clear` says so.

Owed.description: One reaction an actor owes (`act_beat.owed`), with its absolute deadline in epoch ms.

OwedMissed.description: A reaction still owed at the end of the window (`act_done.owed_missed`).

PairKind.description: A pair act between two avatars.

PanelActor.description: One Actor row in the run panel.

PerfectmanUi.description: The `ui_push.ui` union, discriminated by `k`. Also the payload of `ServerMsg::PerfectmanUi`. `Cut` is sidecar to hotel only: the hotel performs it and never forwards it. Every cinematic kind takes an optional `in_ms` delay so the Director's lookahead (D18) can send cues early.

oneOf.description: Built by the hotel from `run_status` and its actor table; the sidecar never pushes it.

llm_p50_ms.description: LLM call latency from the last `run_status` (D53). Absent until the sidecar reports it.

oneOf.description: `code` maps to a localised string; `text` is a literal line (<= 200 chars). One of them is set.
Sidecar to hotel only: move every Audience watcher of the run to `room`.
A wall piece's spot is off its wall, or a floor piece was given one.
Only rugs and the like, and wall pieces, can be brought forward or sent backward.

alive.description: Still in it. Players out of a game stay listed.

PmCmd.description: `start`, `killall` and `open` are hotel-local and never forwarded.

RightsHolder.description: Someone who may edit a room's furniture because its owner said so.

RoomSnapshot.description: The room mirror's first message. `layout.rows`, `walk` and `seats` are server-derived so the sidecar re-implements no rules. The public `Avatar.ai` is never set here (D43).

name.description: Untrusted: the room owner wrote it.

walk.description: `.` blocked or void, `0` open, `s` seat, `g` gate or portal; one string per row.

oneOf.description: The first, second or third twelve, as 1, 2 or 3.

RunBrief.description: One run in the drawer's list (`PerfectmanOpen`).

RunModel.description: An OpenRouter model chosen for one run, with what the hotel knew of it when it was picked.

context.description: Context window in tokens; the sidecar picks the compact prompt for 8192 or less.

price_in.description: OpenRouter's listed price in USD per million tokens, for a model the sidecar has no price for.

reasoning.description: Whether the model thinks before it answers: `mandatory` models get a low effort, `optional` ones are told not to think.

SceneCutReason.description: `scene_cut.reason`: always `sidecar`; the field stays so a later revision can add causes.

ScoreView.description: One row of a game's scoreboard.

cut.description: A cinematic cut: keep the camera, the HUD and the drawers.

spectating.description: You are watching without an avatar (Audience, or a cut): `me` is not in `avatars`.

oneOf.description: Your rights in this room were given or taken back, or you entered a room where you hold them. `can_edit` is what you may now do; `rights` means only furniture, not the settings.
Who holds rights in this room. Sent only to those who may give and take them.

ai.description: Spoken by an AI Actor. Players see the badge; never in Director payloads (D43).

to.description: For a whisper, whom it was to.

untrusted.description: Free text from a stranger that a bot must not treat as an instruction.

oneOf.description: What a bot is told about chat it may not read: who spoke and when, never the text.
Text-bearing mentions a bot did not receive because of the per-sender caps.
Someone did something: a dance, a gesture, a sign or a posture. `stop` ends a dance or a doze. Sent to the whole room, including the one who did it.

ms.description: How long a table gesture plays before the idle pose returns, with no `stop` (TBL-15). Set only by the drama sequencer.

oneOf.description: Every step of your `batch` was applied. `labels` maps each label you gave a placed piece to its id.
Your `batch` changed nothing: these steps (counted from 0) were refused.
A game piece started its show. The client cycles it through its states until the result arrives as a `furni_state_changed`.
What came up at a game piece, for the whole room. `text` is the line to show, and `payout` is what the player got back, always 0 while coins are off.
A moderator removed a picture, so drop it wherever it's showing.
Your coin balance changed. `reason` is `daily`, `active`, `spent`, `refund` or `casino`.
Which games this room allows and the one under way, sent on joining and on every change.

configurable.description: Whether you may switch games on and off here.

oneOf.description: A result or rule announcement from a game, shown like a line of chat.
Sent whether or not the target has blocked you, so a block can't be detected.
Your friends, requests or blocks changed; fetch `/api/friends` again.
The server is ending this connection; the client must not auto-reconnect.
Someone is typing. Sent to the room except the typist.
An admin typed `:pm` with no arguments: open the Perfectman drawer. `start` (from `:pm start` with no scenario) opens it as the start modal, at the scenario picker.
Run panel updates, notices and the cinematic HUD.
The reaction chip: `from` (an Actor id) wants to `kind` you.
"`from` whispers to `to`", for people near a whisper that involves an Actor. Names, not ids: the target may be out of view.
A localisable private notice. `code` maps to a string table; `args` fill its placeholders.
A cinematic run is staged in your room (or you joined one): you are Audience.
The consent chip of an act: `from` (an Actor id) is about to do `verb` to you. Answer with `act_reply` within `ttl_ms`. One chip registry serves this and `pair_prompt`.

default.description: The focused button and the Escape answer: always `dodge`.

oneOf.description: The client steps of an act, compiled by the hotel. Every `at` is in ms from `base_at`.
Ends an overlay early or on its event (the down stand-up, a scene cut).
Drama state for this session: sent on join, on change, and when calm or the pause changes. `enabled: false` hides the opt-in control.

ShotTarget.description: What a shot points at. Externally tagged: `{"avatar":-701}`, `{"pair":[1,2]}`, `{"tile":[3,4]}`, `{"furni":5}`, `{"room":true}`.

ShotZoom.description: A shot's resting zoom: 0.5, 1 or 2, or `"fit"`.

schema_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the vendored `director.schema.json`. A mismatch is logged as a warning; only a `proto` mismatch refuses (checklist 2).

verb_vocab.description: The vendored `verb-vocab.json` of a dialect 2 sidecar (NEG-3, NEG-7).

oneOf.description: Reply to `hello`. `resume` lists the runs the sidecar still holds in memory.

caps.description: `["drama.v1"]` from a dialect 2 sidecar; absent otherwise (NEG-3).

oneOf.description: At least every 5 s per live run, including while paused.
Reply to `run_start`. `ok:false` makes the run `failed`.
Every 5 s per live run. The hotel builds the run panel from it.

lag_ms.description: Event-loop lag of the sidecar, not LLM latency.

llm_p50_ms.description: Median latency of the run's LLM calls over the sidecar's recent window (D53).

oneOf.description: The sidecar finished the run.
`tile: null` spawns on the door tile.

ref.description: The sidecar's agent id; the hotel stores and echoes it, never interprets it.

lease.description: The run's lease. Optional so older sidecars still connect; when present it must be current.

oneOf.description: The sidecar's script advanced: cut the scene. The only way a scene is cut (SCENE-2). With a `cid` a failure answers `actor_error{cid}`; without one it is dropped and logged. Dialect 2 only.

reason.description: Free text, at most 40 characters, logged only.

rows.description: One char per tile: `x` void, `0-9a-w` floor level.

Team.description: Team colours shared by the team games, matching the `_r`, `_g`, `_b` and `_y` pieces.

TimelinePhase.description: Which phase of an act a `act_timeline` frame carries (section 3.11).

TimelineStep.description: A step of an `act_timeline`: `at` is in ms from the frame's `base_at` and may be negative.

oneOf.description: Overlay text in the run's language with `{actor}` and `{target}` already replaced (TBL-13).
The parameters of a `motion` step; which ones are set depends on the motion (section 5.8).

TimeoutAs.description: What silence means on a chip: `dodge`, or the act completing with the initiator's steps only (a hug).

ValidateRequest.description: `POST /authoring/v1/validate`: `source` or `body`. A failing scenario is still `200`.

Verb.description: The 18 verbs (section 0.2). The wire spelling is the table's id.

VerbVocabRef.description: `{version, rev, sha256}` of the published `verb-vocab.json` bytes (NEG-7, VV-3). A `version` mismatch makes the sidecar answer dialect 1; `rev` or `sha256` only warn.
